State-initiated changes: conforming changes due to reorganization/renumbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Utah made conforming changes to existing authorized provisions, primarily internal reference citation revisions due to complete reorganization and renumbering of State regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted under 40 CFR 271.21(a); includes many specific UAC provisions across Chapters R315-15, R315-124, R315-260, R315-261, R315-262, R315-263, R315-264, R315-265, R315-266, R315-268, R315-270, R315-273 (see full listing in the notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: State-initiated changes: amendments that clarify and make regulations internally consistent
rubrics_metrics.description: Utah made amendments that clarify and make the State's regulations internally consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific amendments in Chapters R315-15, R315-124, R315-260, R315-261, R315-262, R315-263, R315-264, R315-265, R315-270, R315-273 (see full listing in the notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: State-initiated changes: conversion from incorporation by reference to verbatim format
rubrics_metrics.description: Revisions associated with the modification to the State's approach from an incorporation by reference format to a verbatim format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive listing of definitional and regulatory provisions across Chapters R315-260, R315-261, R315-264, R315-265, R315-266, R315-268, R315-270, etc., where the State adopted verbatim text of Federal provisions (see full listing in the notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-delegable Federal program areas (limits on state authorization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain Federal functions are purely Federal and not delegable to States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-delegable areas include import/export requirements reserved as part of the Federal foreign relations function, and manifest registry and electronic manifest functions administered solely by the EPA. Utah retained these provisions by leaving the authority with the EPA for implementation and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: State requirement deemed more stringent than Federal
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of State provisions that are more stringent than Federal counterparts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA considers R315-261-420(f)(4)(ii) to be more stringent because the State requires that notification also be given to the Utah Department of Environmental Quality as well as the Federal entities. Utah did not change any previously more stringent or broader-in-scope provisions to be equivalent to the Federal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting responsibilities after authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Who issues and administers permits after EPA authorizes the State program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State of Utah will continue to issue permits for all the provisions for which it is authorized and will administer the permits it issues. EPA will continue to administer any RCRA hazardous waste permits or portions of permits which EPA issued prior to the effective date of this authorization, until Utah has equivalent instruments in place. EPA will continue to implement and issue permits for HSWA requirements for which Utah is not yet authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of authorization on Indian country
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the State authorization extends to Indian country as defined in 18 U.S.C. 1151.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utah is not authorized to carry out its hazardous waste program in Indian country. This includes lands within the exterior boundaries of specified reservations, lands held in trust by the U.S. for Tribes, and any other land qualifying as Indian country. The program revision does not extend to Indian country where EPA will continue to implement and administer the RCRA program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification (what codification means and limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Codification is the process of including the statutes and regulations that comprise the State's authorized hazardous waste management program into the CFR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 3006(b) of RCRA allows EPA to authorize State hazardous waste management programs. The State regulations authorized by EPA supplant the Federal regulations concerning the same matter such that after authorization the EPA enforces the authorized regulations. Infrequently, State statutory language acting to regulate a matter may also be authorized; in that case EPA enforces the authorized statutory provision. EPA does not authorize State enforcement authorities and does not authorize State procedural requirements.
